title: why they do the exact thing we just said not to
body:
why they do the *exact* thing
we just said not to

---

You say "don't touch."
They look right at you…
and touch it.
Slowly.
*Watching your face.*

---

It feels like a test.
Like defiance
with a tiny smirk.

---

But their brain isn't plotting.
It's *practicing.*

---

Ever told yourself "don't check your phone" —
then watched your own hand
pick it up anyway?
Knowing the rule isn't the same
as having the *brake.*

---

They're not defying you.
They're a brain
still building its brakes. 💛

title: 4 things my five-year-old hears when the big feelings hit
body:
4 things my five-year-old hears
when the big feelings hit —
Because one day,
I want them to become
their *own* calm.

---

*"I'm right here."*
Because I want them to know…
a feeling is never too big
to be with someone.

---

*"You're safe."*
Because I want them to know…
the storm always passes.

---

*"It's okay to be sad."*
Because I want them to know…
no feeling makes them
*too much.*

---

*"We'll figure it out together."*
Because I want them to know…
they never have to hold it
alone. 💛

title: when the wrong cup ends the world
body:
when the *wrong cup*
ends the world

---

Blue cup. Not red.
And suddenly they're on the kitchen floor
like something
has actually been *taken* from them.

---

It feels absurd.
It feels like they're winding you up
on purpose,
at 7am,
over a cup.

---

But it was never about the cup.
It was about the *picture*
they had in their head
of how this was going to go.

---

Ever had a day fall apart
because of one small thing
that wasn't even the big thing?
You weren't being dramatic.
The picture just *broke.*

---

They're not fighting you over a cup.
They're grieving a plan
they couldn't tell you
they'd made. 💛

title: "I can't" usually means something else
body:
"I *can't*"
usually means
something else

---

The pencil goes down.
The paper slides away.
"I can't do it."
And you can see
that they nearly could.

---

It's hard not to hear it as giving up.
Hard not to say
"you're not even *trying.*"

---

But "I can't"
is rarely about ability.
It's about the gap
between what they pictured
and what their hand did.

---

Ever abandoned something
you were nearly good at,
because being *nearly* good at it
felt worse
than not doing it at all?

---

They're not quitting.
They're standing
at the edge of hard,
waiting to see
if you think they can. 💛

title: why the worries always wait until bedtime
body:
why the worries
always wait
until bedtime

---

Fine all day.
Lights out —
and suddenly there's a question
about dying,
or a wobbly tooth,
or whether you'll still be here
in the morning.

---

It feels like stalling.
And some nights,
honestly, you're too tired
to be kind about it.

---

But worry needs a *gap* to grow in.
And bedtime is the biggest gap
in a child's whole day.

---

Ever lain in the dark
and suddenly remembered
every awkward thing
you've ever said?
Your brain wasn't broken.
It was just *finally quiet.*

---

They're not delaying bedtime.
They're a busy mind
catching up with itself. 💛

title: why the shoes take nine minutes
body:
why the shoes
take *nine minutes*

---

One shoe on.
Then a conversation with the shoe.
Then the other shoe,
on the wrong foot,
while you stand at the door
holding both your keys and your patience.

---

It feels like they're doing it slowly
*at* you.

---

But a five-year-old has almost no sense
of how long anything takes.
Nine minutes and one minute
feel the *same* from the inside.

---

Ever said "two minutes"
and meant it,
and been genuinely surprised
to look up twenty minutes later?
You weren't lying.
Time just doesn't announce itself.

---

They're not slow on purpose.
They haven't been given
the clock yet. 💛

title: 3 things I say when the friendship goes wrong
body:
3 things I say
when the friendship goes wrong —
Because I want them to have
words for this
long after I'm not in the playground.

---

*"That sounds like it really stung."*
Because I want them to know…
the hurt is allowed to be real
before we fix anything.

---

*"What do you think she wanted?"*
Because I want them to know…
the other child
has a whole story too.

---

*"You don't have to be friends with everyone."*
Because I want them to know…
kind and *close*
are not the same thing. 💛

title: why they save the worst of it for you
body:
why they save
the *worst* of it
for you

---

"She was an angel all day,"
says the teacher.
And then she sees your face
at the gate
and falls apart
before you've reached the car.

---

It lands like a verdict.
Like everyone else
gets the good one.

---

But holding it together all day
costs something.
And they will only ever put it down
somewhere it's *safe* to put down.

---

Ever been perfectly fine at work,
and then cried
at something tiny
the moment you got home?
Home isn't where you fell apart.
Home is where you could.

---

They're not worse with you.
You're the person
they stop performing for. 💛

title: sharing isn't natural, and that's fine
body:
sharing isn't natural —
and that's *fine*

---

The toy has been ignored for six days.
The second another child touches it,
it becomes
the most precious object
ever manufactured.

---

It's embarrassing.
You can feel the other parent
watching how you handle it.

---

But sharing asks a child
to give up something real
for a feeling they can't see yet —
someone *else's* happiness.
That's not selfishness.
That's arithmetic they haven't learned.

---

Ever lent something
you didn't want to lend,
and felt a small hot flare of resentment
even while smiling?
You know the rule.
It still cost you.

---

They're not mean.
They're doing hard sums
with a brain
that's still learning to carry. 💛

title: when "why?" isn't really a question
body:
when "*why?*"
isn't really
a question

---

Why is the sky blue.
Why do we have bones.
Why is that man sad.
Why. Why. *Why.*
Until you'd genuinely pay money
for four minutes of silence.

---

It's hard to stay curious
about a question
you've answered three times
before breakfast.

---

But a lot of the whys
aren't requests for information.
They're requests for
*more of you.*

---

Ever kept a conversation going
past the point of the topic,
because the topic
was never really the point?

---

They're not testing your knowledge.
They're keeping you
in the room. 💛

title: the small change I made to how I praise
body:
I used to say "you're so clever."

It's a lovely thing to say and it costs nothing, which is exactly why it fell out of my mouth so easily. But "clever" is a *thing you are*. And if being clever is who you are, then the moment something is hard, the safest move is to stop — because struggling in front of someone means the label might come off.

So I swapped it for something duller and much more useful: I say what I actually saw.

"You kept going when that got tricky."
"You tried it a different way."
"That took you three goes."

None of it is a compliment, exactly. It's a description. But it points at the part they *chose* rather than the part they were born with — and the part they chose is the part they can do again tomorrow.

It took me an embarrassingly long time to notice that I do this to myself too. I don't need to be told I'm good at something. I need someone to notice that I stayed.

title: a thing worth saying out loud
body:
There is no schedule you are behind on.

There is a version of this that lives on the internet — the reading level, the milestone chart, the other child at the party who is doing something yours isn't — and it is very good at making an ordinary week feel like evidence.

It isn't evidence. It's a photograph of one moment of someone else's life, taken by someone who chose the moment.

Your child is not a project with a deadline. They are a person who is, at this exact moment, mostly interested in whether you noticed the thing they made.

Notice the thing they made. 💛
